title: Moderate Campaign For Constitutional Reforms
definition: The Moderate phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1905) pursued a systematic and peaceful campaign for constitutional reforms, demanding greater representation in legislative councils, extension of the sphere of council activities, and the ultimate realization of self-government within the British Empire through petition, prayer, and protest.
importanceInUpsc: This topic is a high-yield area for UPSC Prelims (evolution of legislative acts, specific moderate leaders, and demands) and Mains GS Paper I (Modern Indian History - spectrum of the freedom struggle, growth of nationalism, and limitations of moderate politics).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Moderate Campaign For Constitutional Reforms.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
